name: S-Class Swashbuckler
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced. The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—a summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

S-class swashbucklers are masters of the sea. With steady legs and keen blades, they perform exceptional deeds.

Role: S-class swashbucklers prefer to stay in melee, but they can get by at close and mid range, and they have the tools and tricks to get out of danger should an enemy think they’re an easy target. When she can line up an exceptional strike, a swashbuckler can be particularly deadly, especially against opponents who can’t pin her down.

Note: The s-class swashbuckler is an alternate, superior version of the swashbuckler class. They retain all of the standard swashbuckler progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select swashbuckler archetypes without specific adjustments.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d10.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp.) In addition, an s-class swashbuckler begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less and her starting weapon (see below).

Class Skills

The s-class swashbuckler’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Table: S-Class Swashbuckler

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class swashbuckler.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

S-class swashbucklers are proficient with simple and martial weapons, as well as light armor and bucklers.

Swashbuckler Style (Ex)

Each s-class swashbuckler chooses a swashbuckler style; a form of combat she prefers to engage in. At 1st level, the swashbuckler’s style gives her an additional way to earn panache (see below). At 2nd, 8th, 14th, and 20th level, she gains benefits specific to her style.

Swashbuckler styles can be found at the end of this section.

Panache (Ex)

At the start of each day, an s-class swashbuckler gains a number of panache points equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1). Her panache goes up or down throughout the day, but usually cannot go higher than her Charisma modifier (minimum 1), though some feats and magic items may affect this maximum. An s-class swashbuckler spends panache to accomplish deeds (see below), and regains panache in the following ways. In addition, the swashbuckler’s style gives her another way to regain panache.

Critical Hit with a Light or One-Handed Melee Weapon: Each time the swashbuckler confirms a critical hit with a firearm attack while in the heat of combat, she regains 1 panache point. Confirming a critical hit on a helpless or unaware creature or on a creature that has fewer Hit Dice than half the swashbuckler’s character level does not restore panache.
Killing Blow with a Light or One-Handed Melee Weapon: When the swashbuckler reduces a creature to 0 or fewer hit points with a firearm attack while in the heat of combat, she regains 1 panache point. Destroying an unattended object, reducing a helpless or unaware creature to 0 or fewer hit points, or reducing a creature that has fewer Hit Dice than half the swashbuckler’s character level to 0 or fewer hit points does not restore any panache.
Deeds

S-class swashbucklers spend panache points to accomplish deeds. At 1st level, 3rd level, and every 4 levels thereafter (7th,11th, and so on), the swashbuckler gains 3 deeds of her choice for which she meets the prerequisites. A complete list of new swashbuckler deeds can be found at the end of this section.

Most deeds grant the swashbuckler some momentary bonus or effect, but there are some that provide longer?lasting effects. Some deeds stay in effect as long as the 2 swashbuckler has at least 1 panache point.

An s-class swashbuckler can only perform deeds of her level or lower. Unless otherwise noted, a deed can be performed multiple successive times, as long as the appropriate amount of panache is spent to perform the deed.

Swashbuckler Finesse (Ex)

At 1st level, an s-class swashbuckler gains the benefits of the Weapon Finesse feat with light or one-handed piercing melee weapons, and she can use her Charisma score in place of Intelligence as a prerequisite for combat feats. This ability counts as having the Weapon Finesse feat for purposes of meeting feat prerequisites.

At 4th level, and again at 10th level, the swashbuckler can select any one type of weapon that can be used with Weapon Finesse (such as rapiers or daggers). Once this choice is made, it cannot be changed. Whenever she makes a successful melee attack with the selected weapon, she adds her Dexterity modifier instead of her Strength modifier to the damage roll. If any effect would prevent the swashbuckler from adding her Strength modifier to the damage roll, she does not add her Dexterity modifier.

Charmed Life (Ex)

At 2nd level, an s-class swashbuckler gains a knack for getting out of trouble. Three times per day as an immediate action before attempting a saving throw, she can add her Charisma modifier to the result of the save. She must choose to do this before the roll is made. At 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the number of times she can do this per day increases by one (to a maximum of 7 times per day at 18th level).

Nimble (Ex)

Starting at 3rd level, an s-class swashbuckler gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC while wearing light or no armor. Anything that causes the swashbuckler to lose her Dexterity bonus to AC also causes the swashbuckler to lose this dodge bonus. This bonus increases by +1 at 2nd, 7th level, and every four levels beyond 7th level (to a maximum of +6 at 19th level).

Bonus Feats

At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, an s-class swashbuckler gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as combat feats. Swashbuckler levels are considered fighter levels for the purpose of meeting combat feat prerequisites.

In addition, upon reaching 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, an s-class swashbuckler can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat she has already learned. In effect, the swashbuckler loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. An s-class swashbuckler can only change one feat at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time she gains a new bonus feat for the level.

Swashbuckler Weapon Training (Ex)

At 5th level, a swashbuckler gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with one-handed or light piercing melee weapons. While wielding such a weapon, she gains the benefit of the Improved Critical feat. These attack and damage bonuses increase by 1 for every 4 levels beyond 5th level (to a maximum of +4 at 17th level).

Swashbuckler Weapon Mastery (Ex)

At 20th level, when a swashbuckler threatens a critical hit with a light or one-handed piercing melee weapon, that critical is automatically confirmed. Furthermore, the critical modifiers of such weapons increase by 1 (x2 becomes x3, and so on).

Swashbuckler Deeds

The following deeds are available to any swashbuckler who meets their prerequisites, if any. When a standard swashbuckler would gain a deed, she can choose one of these deeds instead if it has the same or a lower level prerequisite. Deeds presented in other sources use the level at which they are gained as their prerequisite level when an s-class swashbuckler chooses them.

Note: When one of these deeds refers to a target’s AC, it means that creature’s relevant AC versus the attack, which could be its touch or flat-footed AC in some circumstances.

Allied Feint (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Improved Feint, 7th-level swashbuckler.

The swashbuckler can feint as an immediate action to aid her ally, adding +2 to that ally’s AC against an incoming attack if her check succeeds against the creature attacking it. The swashbuckler can know the result of the attack against her ally before using this deed. If she also has Combat Reflexes, the swashbuckler can use an attack of opportunity instead.

Buckler Expertise (Ex)

As long as the swashbuckler is using a buckler and has at least 1 panache point remaining, she can use a swift action to increase her buckler’s shield bonus to +2 until the start of her next turn. If she spends 1 panache, the swashbuckler can do this as an immediate action instead.

Dagger to the Hand (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Hit the Floor!, 7th-level swashbuckler.

When she uses Hit the Floor!, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point to make a ranged or thrown weapon attack against the triggering creature as part of her immediate action. If her attack hits, the swashbuckler suffers no penalty to her saving throw against a critical hit.

If she has Quick Draw and a free hand, the swashbuckler can draw a ranged or thrown weapon as part of this action, but suffers a –2 penalty to her attack.

Deadly Flourish (Ex)

When she has a weapon drawn, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point and attempt to demoralize an adjacent creature, adding half her swashbuckler level to the check.

Defensive Parry (Ex)

The swashbuckler uses her weapon to shield her body from enemy attacks. As long as the swashbuckler has at least 1 panache point and is wielding a light or one-handed piercing weapon, she gains a +1 shield bonus to her AC. As an immediate action when she’s attacked, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point to add her weapon’s enhancement bonus (if any) to her AC as if it were a shield until the start of her next turn.

Disruptive Ringing (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 3rd-level swashbuckler.

As long as the swashbuckler has at least 1 panache point, she gains the Improved Dirty Trick feat and can perform a dirty trick combat maneuver against an enemy within 5 feet of her any time she makes an attack with a metal, light or one-handed piercing weapon. If the swashbuckler’s combat maneuver check succeeds, the enemy is deafened and unable to make attacks of opportunity until the end of the swashbuckler’s next turn.

The swashbuckler counts as having Improved Dirty Trick and its prerequisites for the purpose of selecting other feats. Unless she meets those prerequisites on her own, she only benefits from the additional feats when she has at least 1 panache point.

Dual-Strike (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Effortless dual-wielding deed or Dex 13, Weapon Focus with a light or one-handed piercing weapon.

When the swashbuckler uses a full-attack action to make multiple light or one-handed piercing weapon attacks against the same opponent in a round, she can spend 1 panache point to total the damage from all hits before applying that opponent’s DR, if any.

Effortless Dual-Wielding (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Dex 15, Two-Weapon Fighting.

As long as the swashbuckler has at least 1 panache point, she treats all one-handed piercing weapons as though they were light weapons when determining her penalties on attack rolls for fighting with two weapons.

Exemplary Finisher (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 15th-level swashbuckler.

When the swashbuckler critically threatens a creature with an attack using a light or one-handed piercing weapon, she can spend 1 panache point as a free action to automatically confirm that critical hit. Performing this deed does not allow the swashbuckler to regain panache from confirming a critical hit or making a killing blow, nor can the swashbuckler use this deed and the Deadly Stab deed on the same attack.

Flesh Wound (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 11th-level swashbuckler.

As a standard action, the swashbuckler can make one attack with a light or one-handed piercing weapon against a creature. If she misses the creature’s regular AC but would hit its touch AC, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point to deal her weapon’s normal base damage as nonlethal damage to the target. The swashbuckler adds only the weapon’s enhancement bonus (if any) to this damage and gains no other benefits that normally come from hitting with an attack.

Gentleman’s Duel (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 3rd-level swashbuckler.

Once per day, the swashbuckler can challenge a foe to combat. As a swift action, the swashbuckler spends 1 panache point and chooses one target within sight to challenge. The swashbuckler’s attacks with light or one-handed piercing weapons deal extra damage when made against the target of her challenge. This extra damage is equal to half the swashbuckler’s level. The swashbuckler can select this deed one additional time at 9th and 15th level. Challenging a foe requires much of the swashbuckler’s concentration. The swashbuckler takes a –2 penalty to her Armor Class, except against attacks made by the target of her challenge.

The challenge remains in effect until the target is dead or unconscious, or until the combat ends.

Hit the Floor! (Ex)

When a ranged attack is made against the swashbuckler, if she is standing and has at least 1 panache point, she can fall prone as an immediate action and attempt a Reflex save DC 10 + the attacking creature’s attack bonus. If the attack would have been a critical hit, the swashbuckler suffers a –4 penalty on her saving throw. If she is successful, the attack misses. She can use this ability even when flat-footed, but not when helpless or unconscious.

Munitions Crafter (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Int 13, Craft (alchemy) 1 rank.

The swashbuckler has developed an understanding of gunpowder and explosives. As a standard action, she can spend 1 panache point to craft and throw a bomb as if she were an alchemist of her swashbuckler level. The swashbuckler’s bombs deal 1d6 fire damage + additional damage equal to the swashbuckler’s Charisma modifier. For every 4 ranks of Craft (alchemy) she has beyond 1, the swashbuckler can select this deed again, increasing her bomb’s damage by 1d6 (this bonus damage is not multiplied on a critical hit or by using feats such as Vital Strike). When she has at least 9 ranks in Craft (alchemy), the swashbuckler gains the fast bombs discovery.

One for All! (Ex)

When an ally the swashbuckler can see who can also see and hear her makes an attack, skill check, or saving throw, or if that ally is being attacked, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point and use aid another on that ally as an immediate action. After you have done this, you can’t do it again for the same ally for one hour.

Overpower (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Piercing Critical, Perception 11 ranks.

As long as the swashbuckler has at least 1 panache point, her attacks with light or one-handed piercing weapons ignore the Damage Reduction of creatures as if they were magic. At 15 ranks in Perception, they ignore DR /cold iron and DR /silver. At 19 ranks in Perception, they ignore DR/adamantine. The swashbuckler must have at least a sliver of the material she wishes to ignore in her possession.

Phalanx Breaker (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 7th-level swashbuckler.

The swashbuckler knows how to break an enemy’s formation with a well-placed attack. When she hits a creature with a light or one-handed piercing weapon, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point and push the target back 5 feet for every 5 by which she beats its AC.

If a target is pushed into another creature, both fall prone. If it’s pushed into a solid object, it takes bludgeoning damage equal to the swashbuckler’s level or her Charisma modifier, whichever is higher.

Perfect Readiness (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 19th-level swashbuckler.

As a standard action, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point to gain the effects of a haste spell for a number of rounds equal to her swashbuckler level. Each time the swashbuckler uses this deed after the first each day, increase the panache points spent to use it by 1.

Piercing Critical (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 7th-level swashbuckler.

As long as the swashbuckler has at least 1 panache point, she gains Improved Critical as a bonus feat for any light or one-handed piercing weapon she wields. If she has that feat for a specific weapon or wields a keen weapon that would otherwise benefit from it, the swashbuckler gains Critical Focus with that weapon instead.

The swashbuckler counts as having Critical Focus and its prerequisites for the purpose of selecting other feats. Unless she meets those prerequisites on her own, she only benefits from the additional feats when she has at least 1 panache point and wields a qualifying weapon.

Quick Strike (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Quick Draw, 15th-level swashbuckler.

When her weapon is stowed, but not hidden or bound, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache as a swift action to draw and attack with that weapon. The target is flat-footed against this attack.

Ride the Rope (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 3rd-level swashbuckler.

With a swipe of her blade or its hilt, the swashbuckler breaks a nearby prop and uses it to gain an advantage on her jump. When she attempts an Acrobatics check to jump, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point and add +5 feet to the result of her jump. This bonus can put the swashbuckler’s jump distance over her movement speed by up to 10 feet. The swashbuckler can know the result of her check before using this deed.

Showstopper (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Twirl and Flourish, 11th-level swashbuckler.

When she uses the Twirl and Flourish deed, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point to compare her feint against all enemies within 30 feet of her that can see the swashbuckler. Each creature against which the check was successful is denied its Dexterity bonus to AC against the next attack made against it by any creature before the end of the swashbuckler’s next turn.

Smoke Curtain (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 3rd-level swashbuckler.

As a standard action, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point to spread a single dose of black powder in front of her and light it, causing a plume of smoke to rise. The plume of smoke billows out from the powder, forming a choking cloud that spreads 20 feet in front of the swashbuckler and lasts for 1 round per swashbuckler level. All sight, even darkvision, is ineffective in or through the cloud. All creatures within the cloud take –4 penalties to Strength and Dexterity (Fortitude DC 10 + 1/2 the swashbuckler’s level + her Charisma modifier negates). These effects last for 1d4+1 rounds after the cloud dissipates or after the creature leaves the area of the cloud. 5

Splinter Ammunition (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Split Ammunition, 7th-level swashbuckler.

When a creature fires the swashbuckler’s split ammunition, it functions as using the Great Cleave feat instead. If the swashbuckler is using the split ammunition, she can also spend 1 panache point at the start of any round during which she intends to fire split ammunition to benefit from any feats she possesses that would require Great Cleave or any of its prerequisites to function, such as All-Consuming Swing, Cleave Through, or Cleaving Finish. The swashbuckler must still possess all other feats required by those feats (for example, Vital Strike).

Split Ammunition (Ex)

Each morning, when a wizard would prepare their spells, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point and designate an amount of ammunition up to her swashbuckler level + her Charisma modifier as split ammunition, making precise cuts on it so that when fired it breaks perfectly in two. Firing split ammunition functions as using the Cleave feat against two targets adjacent to each other. Once created, any creature with a Dexterity score of 13, proficiency with the weapon, and at least a +1 base attack bonus can fire the split ammunition, but it becomes useless to sell. Attacks made with split ammunition only have a chance to misfire on the first attack roll.

Swashbuckler’s Reflexes (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 19th-level swashbuckler, at least 2 deeds that can be used as immediate actions.

The swashbuckler picks two deeds that can be used as immediate actions. Once per round, she can perform those deeds as free actions instead.

Sweeping Blow (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 3rd-level swashbuckler.

The swashbuckler can make a wide, open strike against multiple opponents at a cost. When the swashbuckler makes an attack with a light or one-handed piercing weapon, she can spend 1 panache point and compare her attack against creatures in each of 3 contiguous squares adjacent to her. The swashbuckler then suffers a –2 penalty to AC until the start of her next turn.

Tenacious (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 15th-level swashbuckler.

If the swashbuckler has at least 1 panache point remaining and succeeds on a Fortitude or Will saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, she instead avoids the effect entirely. If she fails, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point as an immediate action to suffer the reduced effect instead.

This ability can only be used if the swashbuckler is wearing light armor or no armor. A helpless swashbuckler cannot gain the benefit from the tenacious deed.

Twirl and Flourish (Ex)

The swashbuckler’s flair can distract her opponent, leaving it vulnerable to her follow-up attacks. As long as the swashbuckler is wielding a light or one-handed piercing weapon and has at least 1 panache point, she can feint in combat as a move action.

Unerring Strike (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 15th-level swashbuckler.

When wielding a light or one-handed piercing weapon, the swashbuckler can spend 1 panache point when attacking a creature against which she would have a miss chance (such as with blur or invisibility) to ignore that miss chance. She must still be aware of the creature and able to pinpoint its space.

Swashbuckler Styles
Battle Dancer

When in battle, you are a mesmerizing performer, dancing along through enemies as they stare, dumbfounded by your erratic movement.

Battle Dance (Ex)

When you roll a natural 20 on a Perform check and succeed, or any time you succeed at a Perform check by 5 or more, you regain 1 panache point. The check must be one you could potentially fail, even if that failure is self-imposed (you choose to increase the DC in some way before making the check).

As a standard action, you can use Perform to feint a creature or move through its threatened squares. If you succeed and the creature is within reach of your melee weapon, you can make a single attack against it as a free action.

Fascinating Performance (Ex)

At 2nd level, when you use Perform to successfully feint or move through a creature’s threatened squares, you can choose another creature you can see that can also see you. If your check result is higher than 10 + that creature’s Sense Motive bonus, it becomes flat-footed until it’s attacked or the end of its next turn. You can only distract each creature in this way once per day.

Bonus Deeds

At 5th and 14th level, you can choose an additional deed for which you meet the prerequisites.

Quick-Step (Ex)

At 8th level, when you would regain a panache point, you can also take a 5-foot step as a free action. At 17th level, any time you take a 5-foot step, you can move up to 10 feet instead (this also allows you to 5-foot-step through difficult terrain).

Leading Dance (Ex)

At 11th level, when you use Perform to successfully feint or move through a creature’s threatened squares and you have at least 10 feet of movement remaining, you can also move that creature up to 10 feet, with you remaining adjacent to it. This movement doesn’t provoke attacks of opportunity. The creature can attempt a Reflex save (DC 10 + 1/2 your level + your Charisma bonus) to halve the distance, ending your movement. Any bonuses to your Perform checks (such as from feats) apply to this save DC.

At 20th level, you can move that creature any distance, up to your speed, but you must declare how far you intend to move it before doing so, and it still receives a Reflex save to halve the distance.

Braggart

You talk a big game, and you have the skill to back it up when you need to.

Proof of Power (Ex)

You can regain panache and perform most swashbuckler deeds while wielding a two-handed bludgeoning or slashing weapon. Deeds that necessitate a free hand still require you to either release, stow, or drop your weapon to perform them.

When you roll a natural 20 on an Intimidate check and succeed, or any time you succeed at an Intimidate check by 5 or more, you regain 1 panache point. The check must be one you could potentially fail, even if that failure is self-imposed (you choose to increase the DC in some way before making the check).

As a standard action, you can attempt to demoralize a creature. If you succeed, and the creature is within reach of your melee weapon, you can make a single attack against it as a free action.

Bonus Feats

At 2nd and 11th level, you gain an additional bonus feat for which you meet the prerequisites.

Heavy-Handed (Ex)

Instead of gaining your swashbuckler’s finesse benefit at 4th level, you can gain Weapon Specialization with a two-handed bludgeoning or slashing weapon for which you have Weapon Focus. At 10th level, you can also gain Greater Weapon Focus with that weapon instead of gaining the benefit of swashbuckler’s finesse.

Braggart’s Edge (Ex)

At 5th level, you gain the Signature Skill feat for Intimidate.

Just as Intimidating (Ex)

At 8th level, when you would regain a panache point, you can also choose one creature you previously tried to intimidate. You can attempt to intimidate that creature again today without granting it any bonuses. At 17th level, if you have at least 1 panache remaining, your first attempt to intimidate any creature each day doesn’t count against you if you fail.

Inherently Intimidating (Ex)

At 14th level, when you would regain a panache point, you also automatically attempt to demoralize an enemy that can see you, even if you’re unaware of its presence. The GM uses 10 + your Intimidate bonus to determine if any such creatures are demoralized by you, beginning with the closest. You don’t also gain panache from this automatic attempt.

At 20th level, you can instead roll Intimidate every time you would regain panache, treating any roll less than 10 on the d20 as 10. Apply your result as described above.

Fencer

You are the swashbuckler others envision when they wish to walk a similar path; a rakish, lightly-armored warrior with a thin blade in hand and a debonair fighting style.

Deceptive Talent (Ex)

When you roll a natural 20 on a Bluff check to feint or create a diversion; or any time you succeed at one of those Bluff checks by 5 or more, you regain 1 panache point. The check must be one you could potentially fail, even if that failure is self-imposed (you choose to increase the DC in some way before making the check).

As a standard action, you can attempt to create a diversion that allows you to hide. If you succeed against each enemy that can see you, you can attempt a Stealth check as a free action to hide, moving up to 10 feet to do so.

Starting at 14th level, you can attempt to create a diversion as a full-round action instead. If you succeed, you and each of your allies those creatures can see can attempt Stealth checks to hide as a free action, moving up to 10 feet to do so.

Fencer’s Duel (Ex)

At 2nd level, you gain the gentleman’s duel deed, even if you don’t meet its prerequisites. You can use that deed when you roll initiative, and you are not limited to using it once per day in this way, but your target gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against attacks made by creatures not participating in the duel. You can still use that deed normally, allowing you to potentially duel two opponents at a time once per day.

Distracting Swordplay (Ex)

At 5th level, when you would regain a panache point, you can also attempt to feint a creature you can see that can also see you as a free action, causing it to be flat-footed against the first attack made by you or one of your allies before the start of your next turn. You don’t also gain panache from this action. After you’ve successfully distracted a creature in this way, you can’t do so again for one hour.

At 17th level, you can apply your attempt to feint against each enemy that can see you, even if you’re unaware of it.

Goading Feint (Ex)

At 8th level, when you successfully feint or create a diversion, the affected creatures also take a –2 penalty to their first attack made before the end of your next turn.

At 20th level, they take that penalty to all attacks they make before the end of your next turn.

You Against the World (Ex)

At 11th level, you can activate gentleman’s duel without spending panache as long as you have at least 1 panache point remaining. You can also activate that deed normally once per minute, and you can choose to grant yourself and any creature participating in the duel a luck bonus up to your Charisma modifier. This bonus applies to attacks and damage against creatures in the duel, and is multiplied on a critical hit. It is the same type of damage as the weapon or spell used in the attack.

Finally, when you use gentleman’s duel, you can designate up to 1 ally and 1 additional enemy to participate, but you can’t have more allies than enemies in the duel at the start, and your ally is no longer part of the duel when only one enemy remains.

Gymnast

More than any other swashbuckler, you weave through battle, performing amazing acts of athleticism and acrobatics.

Gymnastic Athlete (Ex)

When you roll a natural 20 on an Acrobatics, Climb, Escape Artist, or Swim check; or any time you succeed at one of those checks by 5 or more, you regain 1 panache point. The check must be one you could potentially fail, even if that failure is self-imposed (you choose to increase the DC in some way before making the check).

You can choose to make the above skill checks as a standard action. If you do, you add both your Strength and Dexterity modifiers (if positive) to the check.

Flexible Tactics (Ex)

At 2nd level, you can use Acrobatics to perform bull rush, reposition, and trip combat maneuvers, adding both your Strength and Dexterity modifiers (if positive) to the check. You still add bonuses from other feats and abilities, such as Improved Reposition, to those checks. Creatures attempting those maneuvers against you compare their checks against 10 + the above value, if the total would be higher than your CMD.

Deadly Maneuvers (Ex)

At 5th level, when you are wielding a light or one-handed piercing weapon and succeed at an Acrobatics check to bull rush, reposition, or trip an opponent, you can choose to also deal damage as if you attacked it with that weapon. This check has the same critical threat range and multiplier as your weapon, and you confirm any critical threats with a normal attack roll against the target.

At 17th level, you can spend 1 panache point as a free action to either make the successful check a critical threat or automatically confirm it; or you can spend 2 panache points to do both.

Flamboyant Athlete (Ex)

At 8th level, you gain two of the following benefits of your choice. At 14th level, you gain two more. You can choose the same benefit more than once.

You gain a 30-foot climb speed and the +8 racial bonus on Climb checks that a climb speed normally grants. If you already have a faster climb speed, increase it by 10 feet.
You gain a 30-foot swim speed and the +8 racial bonus on Swim checks that a swim speed normally grants. If you already have a faster swim speed, increase it by 10 feet.
You are always considered to have a running start when making Acrobatics checks to jump. If you select this option again, you gain Signature Skill as a bonus feat for Acrobatics.
You ignore up to 5 feet of difficult terrain when using Acrobatics to move through threatened squares.
Clever Acrobatics (Ex)

At 11th level, you count as one size category larger when determining if you can perform a bull rush, reposition, or trip combat maneuver. This doesn’t change any bonuses or penalties you normally have to make those checks.

At 20th level, you count as two sizes larger instead, and opponents larger than your actual size reduce their size bonus to CMD against you by one category (if you’re Small or smaller, Medium opponents take a –1 size penalty to CMD against you).

Wit

Your tongue is as sharp as your blade, and you make excellent use of it both in and out of combat.

Distracting Quip (Ex)

When you roll a natural 20 on a Diplomacy check and succeed, or any time you succeed at a Diplomacy check by 5 or more, you regain 1 panache point. The check must be one you could potentially fail, even if that failure is self-imposed (you choose to increase the DC in some way before making the check).

You can use Diplomacy to feint in combat. If you succeed at an attempt to feint and the creature is within reach of you or an ally wielding a melee weapon, you can grant the result of your feint to yourself or that ally, and you or that ally can make a single attack against the target as a free action.

Opening Feint (Ex)

At 2nd level, you can attempt to feint as a free action when you roll initiative against a creature you can see that can also see you. If you succeed, your targets remain flat-footed to you until the end of your first turn.

At 11th level, you can apply your attempt against up to two qualifying creatures, and at 17th level, you can apply your attempt against each qualifying creature. If you succeed, your targets remain flat-footed to you and your allies until they’re attacked or the end of the first round.

Bon Mot (Ex)

At 5th level, when you successfully feint, targets that become flat-footed also take a penalty on Perception checks and Will saves equal to your Charisma modifier (if positive) while they remain flat-footed.

Uncanny Wit (Ex)

At 8th level, you can attempt to feint creatures with uncanny dodge, but you take a –4 circumstance penalty to your check unless you have at least 4 more levels than their total Hit Dice. You also add your swashbuckler level to your total levels in other classes with uncanny dodge to determine if you can flank an opponent.

Witty One-Liner (Ex)

At 14th level, when you would regain a panache point, you can also choose one creature that can hear you. That creature must succeed at a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 your level + your Charisma modifier) or suffer a –2 penalty to its next attack made before the end of your next turn.

At 20th level, you can force each enemy that can hear you to attempt a Will save instead.
